## TL;DR

Expanded the Android Hub fixture QA sweep from 375px to 360px and 412px, and added explicit lock overlay failure and success retry coverage after review found that the first pass only checked the settings toggle. All 55 fixture checks passed. The mobile build and required scoped RepoOS check passed on this review fix. Browser evidence does not validate a physical Android device or its native biometric prompt.

## Work and rationale

The first pass extended `mobile/scripts/fixture-qa.ts` to run the existing seven UI fixtures at 360px and 412px, exercise the Device lock settings and scope selector, open the edit-server sheet with a long URL, and submit an invalid HTTP URL. It passed at 47/47 checks. Review correctly pointed out that enabling the lock in settings did not actually show the lock screen or exercise retry behavior.

I checked the RepoOS task state and moved #1182 from review back to active through the RepoOS CLI before changing its reviewed worktree. The fix adds a dedicated `lock` fixture with a browser-only verification result selected by the `auth` query parameter. The fixture initializes the normal reopen-lock path. With `auth=failure`, the actual `LockOverlay` appears and `verifyWithDeviceLock` returns false. A retry with the same result leaves the overlay visible. The fixture script then changes only the result parameter to success and retries again; the same retry handler runs, authentication resolves successfully, and the overlay closes. Production authentication logic remains the fallback for all non-fixture URLs.

The lock sequence runs at both viewport widths. It checks that the visible overlay remains within the viewport and that the lock card content has no horizontal overflow. It then confirms the failed attempt keeps the screen locked and the successful retry unlocks it. This closes the specific interaction gap while making no claim about the Android OS biometric prompt, which desktop browser automation cannot drive.

I updated `docs/qa/2026-11-android-hub-second-pass.md` to describe the fixture-driven lock behavior and preserve the distinction between browser evidence and device evidence. The earlier engineer draft was no longer present after the first handoff, so I recreated this report draft with the work and rationale from both sessions. RepoOS can finalize and bind it to the checked tree after the check passes.

## Approaches tried

The first pass attempted the browser UI host, but it was unavailable. The existing Playwright fixture script was already the best repeatable harness, so I used Chromium with the actual Vite app at 360px and 412px. Initially, I considered asserting that the unsupported-device warning appeared when enabling the lock. The browser environment reports the biometric plugin interface as supported, so that assertion was inappropriate. I replaced it with checks for the scope selector and viewport geometry.

For the lock overlay, invoking the native biometric plugin in Chromium would not give a deterministic success/failure result. I used an explicit query-controlled result in the existing dev-fixture module, then drove the rendered UI and Retry button as a user would. Changing the fixture result between retries lets one test establish both the rejected and successful outcomes without stubbing the Vue component or changing native behavior.

## Challenges and blockers

The test proves the Hub's lock overlay behavior and layout in a browser fixture. It does not prove Android biometric prompt appearance, cancellation semantics at the OS boundary, WebView insets, or behavior on a physical device. The earlier server startup also required installing the mobile package's declared dependencies before Vite could resolve Capacitor imports; that was completed in the first pass. No product CSS defect has been reproduced at these widths.

## Key learnings

A settings toggle is not sufficient coverage for a security-related UI flow; tests need to reach the resulting locked screen and cover both rejection and success. Browser fixtures can cover those visible transitions deterministically when the native prompt is unavailable, provided the fixture path stays isolated from ordinary runs. The updated 360px and 412px checks now cover settings, add-server validation, edit-server, offline, and lock overlay states with geometry assertions. A device pass remains the right evidence for native prompt and WebView-specific behavior.
